paper_title: Attributing Response to Context A Jensen-Shannon Divergence Driven   Mechanistic Study of Context Attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
caption: Computational efficiency comparison between our ARC-JSD and Contextcite (n=256 calls) across all datasets and RAG models. Each bar represents the average seconds per sample for ARC-JSD and Contextcite with different RAG models and datasets.

model_annotations.German: This bar chart illustrates a comparison of computational efficiency, specifically seconds per sample, between ARC-JSD and Contextcite across various RAG models and datasets. The horizontal axis represents “Models” with categories labeled Qwen2-1.5B-IT, Qwen2-7B-IT, Gemma2-2B-IT, and Gemma2-9B-IT, appearing in that order. The vertical axis is labeled “Seconds/Sample” with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 80, with tick marks at 0, 20, 40, 60, and 80. For each model category, there are grouped sets of bars representing different combinations of ARC-JSD and Contextcite with specific datasets: ARC-JSD - TyDi QA (blue), Contextcite - TyDi QA (orange), ARC-JSD - Hotpot QA (orange), Contextcite - Hotpot QA (orange), ARC-JSD - MuSiQue (light blue), and Contextcite - MuSiQue (light blue). Within each grouped set, the bars are arranged with ARC-JSD variants first, followed by Contextcite variants. For Qwen2-1.5B-IT, the ARC-JSD - TyDi QA bar is approximately 7 seconds tall, while the Contextcite - MuSiQue bar reaches around 31 seconds. For Qwen2-7B-IT the bars range from approximately 12 seconds to 29 seconds.  For Gemma2-2B-IT, the bars range from around 3 seconds to 14 seconds. For Gemma2-9B-IT, the bars range from approximately 4 seconds to 65 seconds. No bars are visibly emphasized with shading, bolding, outlines, or annotations.
